project.name: Python control-flow exercises
project.summary: Standalone terminal lessons in loops, functions, random choices and branching. Scripts share language concepts, not a runtime database, web API or shared application state.

nodes.label: Prompt and exit loops
nodes.summary: Name and classroom-password loops illustrate continue, break and process exit.

nodes.label: Random choices and games
nodes.summary: Exercises choose random numbers, return fortunes and maintain a rock-paper-scissors score in memory.

nodes.label: Functions and repetition
nodes.summary: Simple greetings demonstrate function calls and arguments; a while loop prints five numbered lines.

nodes.label: Ordered branch examples
nodes.summary: Two fixed name/age examples demonstrate how the first matching if/elif branch wins.

nodes.label: Terminal interaction
nodes.summary: The learner starts each script separately and supplies input or reads output.

edges.label: Answer a prompt
edges.description: Each loop applies its own exact-string condition or exit command.

edges.label: Repeat or finish
edges.description: The selected example prints acknowledgement, echoes input or terminates.

edges.label: Choose a guess or move
edges.description: Number guessing converts input to an integer; rock-paper-scissors validates its move letters.

edges.label: Print feedback and score
edges.description: Games print outcomes; only rock-paper-scissors repeats with cumulative in-memory counters.

edges.label: Print greeting examples
edges.description: These examples require no terminal input.

edges.label: Show the first matching branch
edges.description: Fixed sample data drives the conditional demonstration.

steps.note: Start rpsGame.py and enter rock, paper or scissors using the prompted letter, or quit.
Lowercase and validate the input, select a random computer move, compare moves and increment wins, losses or ties.
Read the outcome and updated counters at the next round. Quit exits the process; scores are not saved.
Start guessTheNumber.py and enter an integer guess.
Compare with a random number from one through twenty; print high/low hints and stop on a match or after six attempts.
Read the success count or the revealed number; noninteger input is not caught.

tour.title: These are separate entrypoints
tour.note: There is no main application dispatcher. yourName.py uses a loop condition; yourName2.py uses an explicit break.

tour.title: Randomness and state are local
tour.note: The guessing target and rock-paper-scissors counters exist only in the chosen script process.

tour.title: Arguments change a greeting
tour.note: helloFunc.py repeats a no-argument greeting three times; helloFunc2.py calls a parameterized greeting for two sample names.

tour.title: Order matters more than the story
tour.note: Each branch example uses fixed sample data. The first matching condition prevents later conditions from being considered.
